arxiv-1502-01287.creator: Stefano Nardulli, Francesco G. Russo
arxiv-1502-01287.description: Abstract . Erdős introduced the noncommuting graph, in order to study the number of commuting elements in a finite group. Despite the use of combinatorial ideas, his methods involved several techniques of classical analysis. The interest for this graph is becoming relevant in the last years for various reasons.

arxiv-2110-12690.title: A Dynamical System Perspective for Lipschitz Neural Networks
arxiv-2110-12690.creator: Laurent Meunier, Blaise Delattre, Alexandre Araujo, Alexandre Allauzen, [0.3cm] Facebook AI Research
arxiv-2110-12690.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Laurent Meunier, Blaise Delattre, Alexandre Araujo, Alexandre Allauzen, [0.3cm] Facebook AI Research. The Lipschitz constant of neural networks has been established as a key quantity to enforce the robustness to adversarial examples. In this paper, we tackle the problem of building 1 1 -Lipschitz Neural Networks. By studying Residual Networks from a continuous time dynamical system perspective, we provide a generic method to build 1 1 -Lipschitz Neural Networks and show that some previous approaches are special cases of this framework.

arxiv-2112-06907.title: Protected hybrid superconducting qubit in an array of gate-tunable Josephson interferometers
arxiv-2112-06907.creator: Constantin Schrade, Charles M. Marcus, András Gyenis
arxiv-2112-06907.description: Abstract We propose a protected qubit based on a modular array of superconducting islands connected by semiconductor Josephson interferometers. The individual interferometers realize effective cos ⁡ 2 ​ ϕ \cos 2\phi elements that exchange ‘pairs of Cooper pairs’ between the superconducting islands when gate-tuned into balance and frustrated by a half flux quantum.

arxiv-2202-04400.title: ℏ \hbar -Riemann–Hilbert correspondence
arxiv-2202-04400.creator: Tatsuki Kuwagaki
arxiv-2202-04400.description: Abstract We formulate and prove a Riemann–Hilbert correspondence between ℏ \hbar -differential equations and sheaf quantizations, which can be considered as a correspondence between two kinds of quantizations (deformation and sheaf quantization) of holomorphic cotangent bundles. The latter category is expected to be equivalent to a version of Fukaya category, which is a “quantization” of Lagrangian intersection theory.

arxiv-2210-04953.title: On Distributed Detection in EH-WSNs With Finite-State Markov Channel and Limited Feedback
arxiv-2210-04953.creator: Ghazaleh Ardeshiri, Azadeh Vosoughi
arxiv-2210-04953.description: Abstract We consider a network, tasked with solving binary distributed detection, consisting of N N sensors, a fusion center (FC), and a feedback channel from the FC to sensors. Each sensor is capable of harvesting energy and is equipped with a finite size battery to store randomly arrived energy.

arxiv-2305-14887.title: Theory of spin-polarized high-resolution electron energy-loss spectroscopy from nonmagnetic surfaces with a large spin–orbit coupling
arxiv-2305-14887.creator: Khalil Zakeri, Christophe Berthod
arxiv-2305-14887.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Khalil Zakeri, Christophe Berthod. The scattering theory of low-energy (slow) electrons has been developed by Evans and Mills [ Phys. The formalism is merely based on the electrostatic Coulomb interaction of the scattering electrons with the charge-density fluctuations above the surface and can describe most of the interesting features observed in the high-resolution electron energy-loss spectroscopy experiments. Here we extend this theory by including the spin–orbit coupling in the scattering process. We discuss the impact of this interaction on the scattering cross-section.

arxiv-2502-11625.title: Comparative Analysis of EMCEE, Gaussian Process, and Masked Autoregressive Flow in Constraining the Hubble Constant Using Cosmic Chronometers Dataset
arxiv-2502-11625.creator: Jing Niu, Jie-Feng Chen, Peng He, Tong-Jie Zhang
arxiv-2502-11625.description: Abstract The Hubble constant ( H 0 \mathrm{H}_{0} ) is essential for understanding the universe’s evolution. Different methods, such as Affine Invariant Markov chain Monte Carlo Ensemble sampler (EMCEE), Gaussian Process (GP), and Masked Autoregressive Flow (MAF), are used to constrain H 0 \mathrm{H}_{0} using H ⁡ ( z ) H(z) data.

arxiv-2510-03681.title: Bayesian Variable Selection for Censored Spatial Responses with Application to PFAS Concentrations in California
arxiv-2510-03681.creator: Suman Majumder, Indranil Sahoo
arxiv-2510-03681.description: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental pollutants of major public health concern due to their resistance to degradation, widespread presence, and potential health risks. Analyzing PFAS in groundwater is challenging due to left-censoring and strong spatial dependence.

arxiv-2602-14838.title: A universal critical accretion rate for black hole jet formation
arxiv-2602-14838.creator: Adelle J. Goodwin, Andrew Mummery
arxiv-2602-14838.description: Abstract It has long been suspected that black hole accretion-outflow coupling is invariant from the stellar to supermassive scales 86 . Stellar mass black hole accretion flows are known to launch jets and outflows as they transition through critical accretion rate thresholds, with values well constrained observationally owing to their short evolutionary timescales.

pmc-11488074.creator: Isabel Nigicser, Fredrik Identeg, Mikael Sansone, Henrik Hedelin, Niklas Forsberg, Ulrika Tranaeus, Klara Edlund
pmc-11488074.description: ObjectivesThe inclusion of rock-climbing in the Olympic Games has increased participation in the sport and attention to athletes' health. In sports where the importance of low body weight is considerate, there is an increased risk of developing eating disorders (EDs). There is sparse research on EDs among rock-climbers.

pmc-12475802.title: Poster 229: Changes in Limb Alignment Following Transphyseal Quadriceps Tendon ACL Reconstruction in Skeletally Immature Patients with 1 or More Years of Growth Remaining
pmc-12475802.creator: Samuel C Willimon, Crystal A Perkins, Anthony C Egger, Michael T Busch
pmc-12475802.description: Objectives:The purpose of this study was to assess changes in limb alignment in skeletally immature patients at 1- and 2-years following transphyseal ACL reconstruction with quadriceps tendon autograft.Methods:A prospective single-center study was performed of all patients less than 19 years of age who underwent transphyseal or conventional ACL reconstruction with an all-soft tissue quadriceps tendon autograft from 10/1/20 – 6/30/22.

pmc-12698900.title: SOX11-mediated CBLN2 Upregulation Contributes to Neuropathic Pain through NF-κB-Driven Neuroinflammation in Dorsal Root Ganglia of Mice
pmc-12698900.creator: Ling-Jie Ma, Tian Wang, Ting Xie, Lin-Peng Zhu, Zuo-Hao Yao, Meng-Na Li, Bao-Tong Yuan, Xiao-Bo Wu, Yong-Jing Gao, Yi-Bin Qin
pmc-12698900.description: Neuropathic pain, a debilitating condition caused by dysfunction of the somatosensory nervous system, remains difficult to treat due to limited understanding of its molecular mechanisms. Bioinformatics analysis identified cerebellin 2 (CBLN2) as highly enriched in human and murine proprioceptive and nociceptive neurons.

pmc-13272439.title: Antiparasitic triterpenic ester and ursolic acid lipid nanocapsule design, cytotoxicity, and permeability evaluation for oral delivery
pmc-13272439.creator: Laura Schioppa, Cecilia Bohns Michalowski, Lucia Mamede, Romano Terrasi, Marie-France Hérent, Giulio G. Muccioli, Raphaël Frédérick, Michel Frederich, Ana Beloqui, Joelle Quetin-Leclercq
pmc-13272439.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionUrsolic acid (UA), the antimalarial triterpenic mixture 8TTE (containing C-27 feruloyl and coumaroyl esters of ursane and oleane skeletons), and the semi-synthetic antitrypanosomal derivative ursolic acid O-phenyl propionate (UAOPP) exhibit high lipophilicity, which may limit their oral bioavailability. This study aimed to develop lipid nanocapsules (LNCs) to improve the solubility, intestinal permeability, and antiparasitic activity of these triterpenic compounds for potential oral delivery.MethodsLNCs formulations containing UA, 8TTE, and UAOPP were prepared and evaluated.

pmc-13312474.title: Accelerometer-derived movement phenotypes and adolescent mental health in pediatric obesity: A causal machine-learning study
pmc-13312474.creator: Siyu Pan, Peng Wang, Fabian Herold, Matthew Heath, Edmund Wei Jian Lee, Effie Lai-Chong Law, Cassandra J Lowe, André Werneck, Markus Gerber, David Moreau, Myrto Mavilidi, Fred Paas, Mats Hallgren, Xia Xu, Liye Zou
pmc-13312474.description: BackgroundChildren with overweight or obesity are at elevated risk for later-life mental health challenges, but the role of accelerometer-derived waking movement behaviors remains uncertain. Thus, we examined longitudinal associations of sedentary behavior (SB), light-intensity physical activity (LPA), and moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity (MVPA) at age 7 with later-life internalizing and externalizing problems.

pmc-13354652.title: Fractional microneedle radiofrequency for photoaging and atrophic acne scar: a split-face clinical observation of two devices
pmc-13354652.creator: Yan Sun, Zi Qing Yu, Ying Zhang, Jin Xuan Wu, Miao Dong, Yuanyuan Xu, Xue Gang Xu, Xing Hua Gao, Shuai Qiao, Yan Wu
pmc-13354652.description: Fractional microneedle radiofrequency (FMR) has been proven effective and safe for acne scar and skin rejuvenation, but the treatment outcomes vary across different FMR devices. The face of each participant was randomly assigned as treatment side (treated with the Peninsula Timerevert Needle) and control side (treated with the EndyMed) along the midline.

pmc-13443947.title: Fostering psychological safety in classroom assessments: moderated-mediation effects of bullying, gender and counselling
pmc-13443947.creator: Theresa Antwi, Patricia Mawusi Amos, Simon Ntumi, John Gabla, Sarah Vivian Davis Chintoh
pmc-13443947.description: Given the growing concern about how school-based bullying undermines students’ academic success and emotional well-being, especially in high-stakes assessment environments, the study investigated the relationships between bullying frequency, psychological safety during assessments, counselling-based accommodations, and academic performance among senior high school (SHS) students in Ghana, with a focus on gender and regional variations.

pmc-13572016.title: Multi-omics reveals that dietary arachidonic acid reshapes hepatopancreatic lipid remodeling and modulates steroidogenesis-related pathways in mud crab
pmc-13572016.creator: Fang Fang, Ye Yuan, Min Jin, Xuexi Wang, Tingting Zhu, Qicun Zhou
pmc-13572016.description: Arachidonic acid (ARA) is a bioactive polyunsaturated fatty acid involved in lipid metabolism, antioxidant defense, and steroidogenesis in aquatic animals. Previous studies have demonstrated that dietary ARA regulates lipid metabolism and steroid biosynthesis in the mud crab Scylla paramamosain. It was hypothesized that dietary ARA promotes steroidogenesis by reshaping hepatopancreatic lipid composition.

pmc-13596241.title: Postoperative complications after Minimally Invasive transCervical oEsophagectomy (MICE) versus Transthoracic Minimally Invasive oEsophagectomy (TMIE): an inverse probability of treatment weighted analysis
pmc-13596241.creator: Justin G A Grootenhuis, Sam Wijers, Gerjon Hannink, Irma Adbegovic, Jasmijn Herruer, Irene F Kramer, Merlijn Hutteman, Sander Ubels, Bastiaan R Klarenbeek
pmc-13596241.description: SummaryMinimally Invasive transCervical oEsophagectomy (MICE) is a novel technique with radical lymphadenectomy that avoids a transthoracic access, potentially preserving pleural integrity and obviating one lung ventilation, thereby reducing postoperative pulmonary complications. However, its advantages over conventional Transthoracic Minimally Invasive oEsophagectomy (TMIE) remain unclear. The objective of this study was to assess postoperative outcomes after TMIE and MICE.
